Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our end: 

- Primary priorities you called out: 95th-pctl latency under 200ms for short queries (<=128 tokens) and steady TPS for batch tagger jobs (target ~180 TPS sustained).
- Shortlist of model variants we discussed (open-source + quantized candidates) attached in the runtime profiles CSV.
- I’m including a small prompt kit (zip) with the prompt templates we ran during the demo and the Redwood-verified TPS/latency snapshot.

Can you confirm the target concurrency and whether the batch tagging will be run during business hours or in a nightly window? That will determine routing and autoscaling suggestions. 

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send the Redwood performance pack + links (attached).
2) If the numbers look good, we’ll schedule a short tech sync with Alex (infrastructure) to map an initial Dedicated capacity estimate.
3) Marissa will follow up with a mutual action plan and procurement checklist if you want to proceed.

Attachments: redwood_runtime_profiles.csv, prompt_kit_v1.zip, tps_latency_snapshot.png

—
Vanessa Ortiz

From: Sam Hudson <sam.hudson@catalystretail.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: runtime profiles, TPS & latency pack, and prompt kit

Vanessa —

Thanks for the recap and the materials. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- Concurrency: initial pilot will be ~8 concurrent users hitting the API for interactive tagging; batch tagging is a separate pipeline targeting 180 TPS but can run outside business hours for now (we might move some to daytime later).
- Latency target: 95th <200ms is ideal. We can accept short bursts above this during peak testing but want a baseline in the steady-state that meets SLA.
- Data residency: US-only. We’ll need the Private option if we go beyond pilot for PII data.

Quick ask: can Redwood share the exact 50th/95th/99th latency percentiles for the recommended model variants and the TPS curves at 1/2/4/8 client connections? That will help us narrow to one candidate. Also want to understand potential quality regressions when using 4-bit quantization — any flags there?

We’re targeting an internal decision by end of next week. If you have the latency/TPS matrix, please send it over and we’ll set up an internal review.

Thanks —
Sam
Director of AI Integrations | Catalyst Retail
sam.hudson@catalystretail.com | +1 212-555-0199

Uploading the numbers you asked for. Attached: redwood_runtime_profiles.csv (per-model 50/95/99 pctl latency at 1/2/4/8 connections) and tps_latency_snapshot.png (curve we captured during the demo load).

Short answers:
- 4-bit quantization: recommended for the lightweight tagger when throughput is the constraint — we’ve seen modest quality drop (1–2% F1) for classification/tagging tasks in our verifications; we include checks in Optimize to run prompt/regression tests when you flip quantization.
- For interactive 8-concurrency target: Model B-Quant (int4) holds ~210 TPS with 95th ~180ms on a g5-like instance (see CSV).

If it helps, I can arrange a short internal runbook review with Alex to map Dedicated capacity and a canary plan for quantization flips.

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo: runtime profiles, TPS & latency pack, and prompt kit

Vanessa / Marissa —

Reviewed the CSV and the snapshot. High-level answers below (short, actionable):

- Validation: the CSV numbers look consistent with our Verified profiles for the March build. Quick summary:
  * Model A (base int8): 8-concurrency 95th = 165ms, 99th = 230ms, steady TPS ~160.
  * Model B (optimized int8 / int4 candidate): int8 95th = 195ms, int4 95th = 185ms, int4 steady TPS ~210 at 8 connections (note: int4 shows slightly lower 99th tail variability on the April kernels due to improved KV cache handling).
  * Model C (larger contextual model): higher latency; 95th ~420ms at 8-concurrency — not recommended for interactive pilot.

- Regression risk for int4: for token classification/tagging tasks we’ve observed a small F1 delta (0.01–0.03) compared to int8 when prompts are short and the model is finetuned. If Catalyst’s labeling tolerances are tight, recommend running our Optimize prompt-regression suite (we can run it against their sample dev set) before flipping to int4 in production.

- Dedicated sizing & fallback: For the pilot (8 interactive + nightly 180 TPS), recommend 2 x g5-like nodes with autoscaling policy (scale-to-2 baseline, burst +1 during nightly batch). Fallback policy: primary int4 variant -> int8 variant (same model) -> smaller Model A if memory constrained.

- Next steps I can take this week: spin up a short accuracy/regression run with their sample prompts (if Catalyst shares dev set) and provide a one-page ops runbook for canary flips (quantization gates, health checks, trace sampling).

I’ll drop the one-pager to Drive and link it here when done: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-prompt-kit-catalyst (will add file: canary_runbook_Catalyst.pdf).

—
Alex Martinez
